text: CMV disease, pre-emptive therapy with either intravenous ganciclovir or foscarnet rather than primary prophylaxis, is the recommended ap- proach. Intravenous ganciclovir is, however, effective for primary prophylaxis but should be reserved for patients at high risk of developing disease. Aciclovir or valaciclovir may also be used for primary prophylaxis but their use must be combined with monitoring and pre-emptive ther- apy with either intravenous ganciclovir or foscarnet. If, however, ganciclovir has been given for primary prophy- laxis then foscarnet should be used for first-line pre-emp- tive therapy. The use of valganciclovir for primary proph- ylaxis is under investigation, but if it is given then foscarnet should be used subsequently for first-line pre- emptive therapy. Cidofovir may be used as second-line pre-emptive therapy.23 CMV vaccines are currently in development. 1. CDC.
